title: Silver-Copper Nanocoating on Medical Grade Plasticized Polyvinyl Chloride Substrates: Physico-Chemical Properties and  Antibacterial Efficacy
content: Polymeric materials such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC) are frequently used in medical and dental facilities, where they are frequently exposed to environmental pathogens. This microbial contamination poses a significant risk to patient safety. To address this concern, we evaluated the physicochemical and antibacterial properties of a bimetallic silver-copper (Ag-Cu; SakCu®) nanocoating deposited onto medical-grade PVC by magnetron sputtering at thicknesses ranging from 15 to 50 nm. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) revealed a uniform, continuous polycrystalline coating. The deposition process preserved the substrate's integrity. Tensile testing demonstrated that the coated PVC retained 65%–82% of its original maximum load, while FTIR spectroscopy revealed no chemical changes in the polymer. Biological assays showed that Ag-Cu-coated PVC significantly inhibited surface colonization, achieving greater than 90% growth inhibition against representative Gram-positive and Gram-negative nosocomial pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus epidermidis. These findings indicate that Ag-Cu nanocoatings can be applied to medical-grade PVC without compromising its versatile properties, offering a promising approach to preventing biofilm formation and reducing healthcare-associated infections in clinical settings.
